authoredNote: line_number values transcribed from a measured run of the production entry (parseFile) and checked against the numbered source: `double(21)` is on line 34, `double(length(local.merged))` on 42 and `double(2)` on 46, each being the line the CALLEE IDENTIFIER is written on (the same convention every other edge in this analyzer uses — the site, not the declaration start). The `references` rows on lines 38 and 42 are the address read INSIDE a call, and the fact that line 42 carries both a `calls` and a `references` edge is the point of the nested line. The `calls` forbids were authored BEFORE the run from the source: merge(…) and length(…) are written in the fixture and are Terraform globals, so before this change a rule keyed on 'any function_call' would have published them.
rationale: HCL has no function-declaration production: a function is a block, and the ecosystem layers the declaration on top of the container grammar. docker-bake spells that `function "name" { … }` and Terraform 1.8+ spells it `func "name" { … }`; both parse as an ordinary one-label block, which is why a block-driven walker reaches them with no grammar support. Measured over 9,329 corpus files / 2,035,319 nodes: exactly ONE declaration of the shape exists — `function "bindir"` at docker/docker-bake.hcl:56 — with 4 call sites (lines 101, 106, 137, 151), and `func` occurs 0 times. Everything else is a global: 12,968 unqualified `function_call` nodes over 139 distinct callees plus 20 namespaced `provider::` calls over 9 callees, none of which any file declares. So `calls` is emitted ONLY where the same file declares the callee, which is what keeps every `calls` edge resolvable and stops a fake caller becoming wrong advice in bb_graph and bb_impact. The target is the declaration's index identity (`function.double`), not the bare name the file writes, because that is the string the index can bind; the call-site spelling rides along in metadata.hclCallee so nothing is lost.

expectSymbols.name: function.double
expectSymbols.note: the declaration is an ordinary nested block — the `function` spelling is a dialect convention, not a grammar production — so `class` stays and `hclFunctionDecl` is what tells a consumer this block is callable

expectSymbols.name: function.unused
expectSymbols.note: declared and never called. An uncalled declaration is still a declaration, and dropping it would make the symbol set depend on call sites.

expectSymbols.name: params
expectSymbols.note: `params = [n]` is a collection_value wrapping a tuple; `hclValueKind` names the node that describes the value and only unwraps `operation`, so this is the honest spelling

expectSymbols.name: result
expectSymbols.note: `n * 2`: the `operation` wrapper is unwrapped so a comparison or an arithmetic expression is reported as the operation it is

expectRelationships.note: the only shape that becomes a call edge: a callee a `function` block in this same file declares. The target is the declaration's index identity, which is what resolves; the call-site spelling is kept in hclCallee.

a declared function NESTED inside a global call — `double(length(local.merged))`. The callee of the outer call declares nothing, the callee of the inner one does, and the two are different facts on the same line.
a call from a resource block: the SOURCE is the enclosing block's qualified path, the same convention every other relationship in this analyzer uses.
the reference read INSIDE the call is still published. Calling a function and reading an address are different facts and the analyzer keeps both straight.
